brief: Zero Hedge's daily wrap argues credit cracks are starting to drive equity risk. Widening data-center bond spreads, CoreWeave debt near 85 cents, tripled megacap-tech CDS, and a $5bn Volta loan that JPMorgan and Goldman underwrote only partly feed doubts that AI capex can earn an adequate return, which pressures forward earnings estimates and valuations for the AI-led equity leadership. That shows up in options positioning: Nasdaq gamma has flipped negative, amplifying moves, while SPX stays buffered between 7,700 and 7,800. A break below that line could turn the AI-trade wobble into a broader correction. Separately, oil whipsawed as a Russia-Ukraine energy-ceasefire collapsed (Russia struck Ukrainian power plants, sending diesel prices up) and the Saudi-Houthi conflict escalated, even as OPEC cut its 2026 demand-growth forecast to about 400,000 bpd from 1.4 million. Diesel cracks near $100 and record tanker rates leave Brent, per Bloomberg's Monkam, vulnerable to a catch-up higher. Fed speakers split: Goolsbee and Barkin flagged AI demand overheating the broader economy and lifting inflation, while Williams still expects one more 2026 hike but none in 2027. December hike odds rose to cycle highs near 90%.
